question: Across the whole week in this data, which departure was the latest, and what was it blamed on?

content.text:
**WN4285, SDF–BWI, scheduled 05:40 local on 2026-01-01** (`2026-01-01|WN|4285|SDF|BWI|0540`, tail **N291WN**) pushed back **692 minutes late** — 11h32m. It is the only departure in the week over 600 minutes late; the next worst is WN1278 BOS–BWI on 01-04 at 458 minutes (`2026-01-04|WN|1278|BOS|BWI|1740`).

It arrived BWI 677 minutes late, and the carrier attributed **all 677 minutes to carrier cause** — zero weather, zero NAS, zero security, zero late-aircraft. That attribution is consistent with the rotation: `previous_leg` is empty, so this was N291WN's first leg of the day and none of the delay was inherited from an earlier flight. What the "carrier" bucket actually covers here (maintenance, crew, ground handling) is not recorded in this extract; BTS gives only the five cause buckets.

Downstream exposure was small because the tail only flew one more leg: `2026-01-01|WN|1732|BWI|MCI|1930` went out 34 minutes late, of which **18 minutes were booked as late_aircraft** — the scheduled 00:30 UTC departure sat only 58 minutes after the 23:32 UTC arrival, so the 677-minute arrival delay was almost entirely absorbed by the long scheduled ground time. That leg arrived MCI 38 minutes late and the rotation ended there.
